core_obligations: Reduce to one algebra: the centre having order two, the proof observes that only one Tits algebra has to be considered and that R-universality requires it to be either trivial over the rationals or non-trivial over the reals (proof lines 834-836).

Read off the classification: the author then quotes the tabulated behaviour of that algebra for the listed indices, distinguishing the indices where it is trivial from those where it is non-trivial (proof lines 836-839).

The anisotropic case: since there are no strongly inner anisotropic groups of type E7 over the fields in question, the Tits algebra is also non-trivial for the anisotropic algebra listed, which completes the list of alternatives (proof lines 839-841).
Conclusion: the two alternatives of the statement (proof line 841).
proof_roadmap: 由 E7 的单连通群中心为 2 阶，只需一个 Tits 代数；R-universality 等价于它在 Q 上平凡或在 R 上不平凡。
再引 Tits 的分类：E^{28}_{7,3}、E^0_{7,7} 上平凡，E^{31}_{7,2}、E^9_{7,4} 上不平凡；又因 E7 在 Q 与 R 上无强内各向异性群，E^{133}_{7,0} 的 Tits 代数也不平凡。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the R-universality criterion for the absolutely simple algebras of type E7 (author prop at source lines 823-831), which reduces to the behaviour of a single Tits algebra and is stated as a list of Tits indices. The proof (source lines 833-842) is short: the order-two centre reduces the criterion to one algebra (proof line 834), the classification supplies its behaviour for each index (proof lines 836-839), and the absence of strongly inner anisotropic forms of type E7 covers the anisotropic case (proof lines 839-841). The turn from the invariant to the index list is the whole content. H2.
